chapter: New Orleans clarinetists and learning the guitar
title: George Baquet and the clarinet funeral style
summary: George Baquet played funerals with Manuel Perez's brass band; comparison with Piron and Alphonse Picou; Bechet sleeping in the market.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Do you remember George Barquet, the one that played with your brother? Can you tell us anything much about him? Do you remember George?

George Barquet. Yeah, I played with him. George was a good clarinet player, too. And he is a player of funerals. And he was a funer man. He didn't miss a lick. He was right there on the job. Well, I tell you, if I am mistaken, I believe he was a better musician. Not in the line of musician, but in the line of playing, I believe he was better than Alphonse Piku. In a funeral. Because he used to play some tough music, and he used to make that clarinet cry like a baby. He was solid. He was good. Of course, Piku is all right, but he's variation. But George used to put on this lead improvisation, you know? And that lead is the main thing, and put everything in its place. And I remember seeing students where George used to blow that clarinet with his head up in the air, and George taking head people around that crime.
That's what I've heard other people, too, and told me that, too.

And that song, I'll never forget that song, but I don't know exactly the words, but I sure would like to know the words of that. But I can always hum the words. And what's it like? If you don't mind, I'll hum the words.
It goes like this. It's gosh, gosh, gosh. I
I I I I I I I I I

I George with that clarinet, he'd make them what they call shriveling that clarinet. And Mario Perez, he was playing with Mario Perez's brass band. And Mario used to be the leading and he used to be making nothing but just crying in that clarinet. Of course I understand.
But it was a slow funeral of dirt.

No, I remember four times. Yeah. Flow four. Now, Mario would make the lead. Of course they used Pico and all that, but now and that, but they didn't lead no more than him. And he used to have that clarinet going. Now another one he was good too, and he was clumsy, Lorenzo Teo. He was tough. His daddy was alright, but not like Lorenzo Teo. See but the whole thing is Lorenzo Teo, he was just like Bechet. Bechet is one of them. He was a good clarinet. Of course I understand. He went away and he played for the Queen, the King and everything else. He was a clarinet player. But he was a clarinet player. And he used to have rubber, just like Lorenzo Teo used to have rubber on the clarinet when he come to play on the job. He's clarinet full of rubber. But Bechet takes a while. My piece and play this by himself. Don't need the whole stick. Somebody else tell me that. See? Of course he used to take and be, he used to be in that market. He used to sleep on the meat stand. You know they had a market there right there on the Seminar and Flavorne before that grocery went there. That's a circle there. But it used to be a meat stand there. It was. I didn't know. How about that grocery? How was that in there? Well, there was a meat stand. They had butchers up in there. And then, of course, since this man bought it, well he put his gross up in there. Now they call it the circle. The, I mean the circle market. But that was nothing but a big butcher stand. So of course Bechet used to be up in there. And they used to have an alley back there. Well, that pig, they probably used to shine shoes back there. And Bechet used to sleep on the stand back there. Wouldn't even go home to sleep. Wouldn't go home. Of course, I don't know if he had a home. I don't know at that time he was young, you know. And of course the boys was mischievous. But they ain't bad like they is now. They'd go and rest theirself and go lay down somebody, around somebody. But now they don't rest until they get a hold of a pocketbook.
Unless they knock your brains loose.
If you got them, if you ain't got them, they'll knock your brains loose, you know. Can you tell us anything about the Block A family?
